chunks: Al-Ḥusayn ibn Muḥammad, from Muʿallā ibn Muḥammad, from ʿAlī ibn Muḥammad, from Bakr ibn Ṣāliḥ, from al-Rayyān ibn Shabīb, from Yūnus, from Abū Ayyūb al-Khazzāz, from Abū Ḥamzah, who said:

Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام said: “O Abū Ḥamzah, one of you travels farsakhs and seeks a guide for himself, while regarding the paths of the heaven you are more ignorant than you are regarding the paths of the earth; so seek a guide for yourself.”

key_terms.أَجْهَلُ: more ignorant; less knowledgeable and in greater need of instruction
key_terms.دَلِيلًا: a guide who shows the correct path
key_terms.طُرُقِ السَّمَاءِ: the paths of heaven, meaning the way to divine guidance and salvation
key_terms.طُرُقِ الْأَرْضِ: the paths of the earth, meaning ordinary worldly routes
key_terms.فَرَاسِخَ: long distances of travel, used here to illustrate worldly caution in seeking direction

ai.seo_question: Why does Imam Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام say a believer must seek a guide for the path to heaven?
ai.summary: This hadith teaches that just as a person seeks a guide for travel in worldly paths, he is even more in need of guidance in the far more consequential path leading to the heavens. Its significance lies in directing the believer to recognize the necessity of divinely appointed guidance, especially the Imam عليه السلام, in matters of religion and ultimate salvation.

en.hubeali: Al Husayn Bin Muhammad, from Moalla Bin Muhammad, from Ali Bin Muhammad, from Bakr Bin Salih, from Al Rayyan Bin Shabeeb, from Yunus, from Abu Ayoub Al Khazzaz, from Abu Hamza who said,

‘Abu Ja’farasws said: ‘O Abu Hamza! (When) one of you goes out for one Farsakh, so he is seeking a navigator for himself, and you are more ignorant of the ways of the sky than the ways of the earth, therefore seek a navigator for yourself’.
en.sarwar: 10. Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad has narrated from Mu‘alla ibn Muhammad from Ali ibn muhammad from Bakr ibn Salih from al-Rayyan ibn Shabib from yunus from abu Ayyub al-Khazziz from abu Hamza who has narrated from Imam abu Ja’far‘far (a.s.) the following.

“O abu Hamza, when one of decide to travel for just a few miles he first finds a guide and direction for himself. Your knowledge of the paths of heavens is much less than your knowledge of the paths of earth. You must find a guide for yourself.”
